I've been working this land for 28 years. I know Quzhou's soil and climate — dry springs, hot summers, cold winters. My well saves me every time the rains fail, which is often.

My main system is cabbage-chili rotation. The same 2.5 mu carries cabbage in autumn, then I turn it over to chili in spring. That rotation keeps the soil from getting too tired of one crop. My remaining 1 mu I split between eggplant and kidney bean — eggplant sells well at the summer market in town, and kidney bean my family eats plus I sell what's left.

For seeds, I buy hybrid cabbage, hybrid chili, and hybrid eggplant every year from the county seed store. The hybrids cost more but the yield is better and the heads are uniform — buyers pay better for that. For kidney bean I still use seed I saved from last season. It does fine and I'm not spending money on something that doesn't need it.

Fertilizer — I apply compound fertilizer as base before transplanting, then top dress urea and potassium during the growing period. I've learned from my father and from doing it myself what these fields take. I don't bother with soil tests; I can tell from the leaf color and growth.

Irrigation from my well — chili and eggplant drink the most in summer heat, cabbage less so in the cooler months. I water by experience, not by schedule.

Pesticides — I spray on a schedule and when I see pests. Cabbage gets aphids and caterpillars. Chili gets spider mites and anthracnose. I rotate products a bit so they don't stop working.

All fields get rotary tilling before planting. I rent the machine from a neighbor.
